frozenRule.protocol: Fixed 168-point BattleCats-selected lexical grid; frozen prior to holdout evaluation

historical_426_corpus.nature: Synthetic partial queries generated as two-word suffix tails of longer field names
historical_426_corpus.finding: Deterministic lexical screen outperformed Jev on synthetic benchmark because queries directly matched field suffix tokens.

sparkle_xadmaster_freeform.nature: Human-authored natural language reverse-engineering queries describing semantic intent without identifier leakage

deterministicPlusJev.rule: Deterministic screen gates Jev only if deterministic confidence margin > threshold
deterministicPlusJev.finding: Deterministic screen is ineffective for free-form intent queries; gating Jev behind lexical matching actively blocks valid semantic rescues.

conclusion: The strong performance of deterministic lexical screening on the 426 corpus was an artifact of synthetic query generation bias (two-word suffix tails). On genuine human free-form reverse engineering queries, deterministic lexical screening collapses (0/3 on key regression cases) because natural phrasing describes behavioral purpose rather than naming identifiers. Jev provides genuine semantic comprehension that deterministic rules cannot replicate, but requires class context (Arm C/D) to avoid lexical traps.
